title: Mechanism of Atractylodis Rhizoma in improving cognitive dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease by regulating the cAMP/CREB/BDNF pathway.
authors: Xu, Xinlin; Zhao, Yinan; Ma, Huifen; Hu, Yilong; Yu, Linyu; Su, Yunfang; Song, Junying; Xie, Zhishen; Zhang, Zhenqiang; Wang, Pan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药白术乙醇提取物通过cAMP/CREB/BDNF通路改善阿尔茨海默病认知障碍，核心为疾病机制与药物作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，且方法以实验为主，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive, debilitating condition with substantially limited therapeutic options. Atractylodis Rhizoma, a spleen-invigorating herb in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), shows promise for AD, but its mechanisms are unknown. METHODS: Chemical constituents of the ethanol extract of Atractylodis Rhizoma (EEAR) were identified via UHPLC-HRMS and followed by network pharmacology integrated with molecular docking to predict putative therapeutic targets. An AD rat model was established by bilateral intracerebral stereotaxic injection of Abeta(2)(5)-(3)(5). Cognitive function and neuronal damage were evaluated using behavioral tests and Nissl staining. Levels of key pathway components were measured by ELISA, RT-qPCR, and Western blotting, and inflammatory factors were measured by ELISA. RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) and in vitro experiments were conducted to validate EEAR's regulatory effects on the key signaling pathway. RESULTS: EEAR administration ameliorated cognitive deficits and attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage in AD rats. Notably, EEAR markedly reduced the concentrations of IL-6, IL-1beta, and TNF-alpha in the rat hippocampus, concomitant with upregulation of the cAMP/CREB/BDNF signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis confirmed significant enrichment of DEGs in the cAMP signaling pathway in the EEAR-H. In vitro, EEAR protected HT22 cells against Abeta(2)(5)-(3)(5)-induced injury, and the CREB-specific inhibitor KG-501 effectively blocked EEAR-induced activation of the cAMP/CREB/BDNF pathway. CONCLUSION: EEAR mitigates AD pathogenesis by directly targeting hippocampal neuroinflammation and potently activating cAMP signaling, establishing its potential as a multi-target therapeutic candidate and providing a scientific basis for traditional medicine-derived AD interventions.
abstract_zh: 背景：阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种进行性、使人衰弱的疾病，治疗选择极为有限。白术（Atractylodis Rhizoma），一种在中医（Traditional Chinese Medicine, TCM）中用于健脾的草药，对AD显示出潜力，但其作用机制尚不清楚。方法：通过UHPLC-HRMS鉴定白术乙醇提取物（EEAR）的化学成分，并结合网络药理学与分子对接预测潜在治疗靶点。通过双侧脑内立体定向注射Abeta(2)(5)-(3)(5)建立AD大鼠模型。使用行为测试和尼氏染色评估认知功能和神经元损伤。通过ELISA、RT-qPCR和Western blotting测量关键通路成分的水平，并通过ELISA测量炎症因子。进行RNA测序（RNA-Seq）和体外实验以验证EEAR对关键信号通路的调控作用。结果：EEAR给药改善了AD大鼠的认知缺陷并减轻了海马神经元损伤。值得注意的是，EEAR显著降低了大鼠海马中IL-6、IL-1beta和TNF-alpha的浓度，同时上调了cAMP/CREB/BDNF信号通路。RNA-seq分析确认了EEAR-H中差异表达基因在cAMP信号通路中的显著富集。在体外，EEAR保护HT22细胞免受Abeta(2)(5)-(3)(5)诱导的损伤，且CREB特异性抑制剂KG-501有效阻断了EEAR诱导的cAMP/CREB/BDNF通路激活。结论：EEAR通过直接靶向海马神经炎症并强效激活cAMP信号来缓解AD发病机制，确立了其作为多靶点治疗候选药物的潜力，并为源自传统医学的AD干预提供了科学依据。
